title: CReal.evt_approx_max: the Extreme Value Theorem's honest row 1 -- an approximate maximum
statement: Let F be an arbitrary uniformly continuous real function on [a, b] with a <= b. Then for EVERY accuracy index n, there exists x in [a, b] such that for every y in [a, b], F y <= F x + 1/(n+1) -- an APPROXIMATE maximum, exact structural mirror of CReal.ivt_approx (ADR-0603 row 1 for IVT). Pure composition of CReal.supOn_approx_lub (the witness x, within 1/(n+1) of the supremum) and CReal.supOn_ub (every F y is at most the supremum) through CReal.le_trans -- no new supremum machinery. This is NOT an attained maximum and does not narrow CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign at all: the witness x moves with n and is never claimed to converge to a limit. F must still be assumed UniformlyContinuousOn [a,b] with an explicit modulus carried as Sort 1 data, the same restriction CReal.ivt_approx and every rung of the supremum construction carries.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.evt_approx_max : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal.le x1 x2) -> ((x4 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x1 x2) -> ((x5 : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} CReal (fun (x6 : CReal) => And (CReal.le x1 x6) (And (CReal.le x6 x2) (((x7 : CReal) -> ((x8 : CReal.le x1 x7) -> ((x9 : CReal.le x7 x2) -> CReal.le (x0 x7) (CReal.add (x0 x6) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x5)))))))))))))))

notes: Registered by lane evt-row1-land-and-register, correcting a stale absence claim in ADR-0692 and docs/formalized-math-2026-08/08-ivt-and-evt-measured-against-mathlib.md Section 2: both said EVT's row 1 was missing, but the two theorems this declaration composes (CReal.supOn_ub, CReal.supOn_approx_lub) already existed under those exact names -- the absence probe in both documents searched for a guessed name, CReal.supOn_upper_bound, which never existed. See ADR-0895 for the full history and the negative control (the slack term 1/(n+1) cannot be dropped: the exact form is refuted by CReal.evt_attained_max_decides_sign). This theorem does NOT make EVT Pareto-dominant over Mathlib's IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn: ours concludes an approximate bound, Mathlib's an exact attained maximum, and the two-axis dominance test's verdict on that comparison is left to a future revisit of the axis tables in 08-ivt-and-evt-measured-against-mathlib.md.
